Geographic focus:
    Australia (Northern Territory / Beetaloo Basin), Middle East (Iran, Qatar, Strait of Hormuz), Asia (China, Japan, Indonesia)

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [YES] — covers LNG export history, Qatar disruption, Beetaloo development timeline
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — spot LNG price spike, Qatar cargo disruption ongoing
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — Beetaloo infrastructure build-out, Asian gas demand growth +30% over 10 years, Australia LNG export expansion

Synopsis:
    Australia's remote Beetaloo shale basin is gaining strategic urgency as the Iran conflict (started Feb 28, 2026) disrupts Middle East LNG flows, particularly from Qatar. Spot LNG prices have surged ~150% to $25.80/MMBtu. With at least 200 tcf of recoverable gas, Beetaloo could transform Australia into a dominant LNG supplier for Asia, benefiting from geographic proximity and no Hormuz exposure. Key operators include Tamboran, Inpex, and Santos, but critical infrastructure decisions remain unresolved. The article frames this as a geopolitical inflection point for Asian energy security.

Marginal indirect relevance exists via energy inflation pass-through and the mention of US LNG as a comparable benchmark.
